extracted.intended_audience: Covered entities and stakeholders subject to Section 1557 (health care providers, health plans/payers, developers of clinical decision support tools, compliance officers, legal counsel, and policy stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for complying with Section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations in health programs and activities, including rules specific to patient care decision support tools and telehealth accessibility, and the enforcement procedures OCR will use.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on discrimination via patient care decision support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §92.210(a) (General prohibition) — prohibits discrimination resulting from covered entities' use of patient care decision support tools; replaced term “clinical algorithm” with “patient care decision support tool.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to automated or non-automated tool[s] . . . used by a covered entity to support clinical decision-making. OCR is concerned about discriminatory bias introduced in real-world post-market deployment and emphasizes identifying points of bias and providing an action plan for remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing duty to identify decision support tools that employ inputs measuring protected characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.210(b): “A covered entity has an ongoing duty to make reasonable efforts to identify uses of patient care decision support tools in its health programs or activities that employ input variables or factors that measure race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities must identify uses of tools in their health programs/activities when input variables or factors measure protected characteristics. Identification is an ongoing duty; OCR will evaluate whether a covered entity appropriately identified its use of such tools during investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risk from identified tools
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.210(c): “For each patient care decision support tool identified in paragraph (b) of this section, a covered entity must make reasonable efforts to mitigate the risk of discrimination resulting from the tool's use in the covered entity's health programs or activities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires covered entities to adopt mitigation actions for each identified tool. OCR will determine whether mitigation efforts were reasonable as part of case investigations. Mitigation planning should include identifying points of bias and remediation steps; OCR will use all available means (complaint investigations and compliance reviews) to assess compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness standard scaled to entity size and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance obligations (e.g., identifying tools and mitigating risk) require covered entities to make “reasonable efforts,” and the size and resources of the covered entity will factor into the reasonableness of those efforts and their compliance with §92.210.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges that smaller entities may face greater difficulty and will factor size and resources into enforcement/assessment of what constitutes ‘reasonable efforts.’ This scaling affects both identification and mitigation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No strict liability imposed on covered entities for use of decision support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to impose strict liability on covered entities for discriminatory outcomes from use of patient care decision support tools; a covered entity's liability under Section 1557 is independent of, and not contingent on, a developer's potential liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a developer is itself subject to Section 1557, §92.210 applies to it as it applies to other covered entities. OCR will not treat covered entities as strictly liable simply because they use a tool; instead OCR examines whether they took requisite steps under §92.210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on patient care decision support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities should refrain from over-relying on patient care decision support tools by using them beyond their reasonably expected scope as a replacement or substitute for providers' clinical judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overreliance can result in discrimination. §92.210 addresses the covered entity’s use (not 'reliance') of such tools; OCR cautioned that overreliance in decision-making may lead to discriminatory outcomes and will be considered in investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative approach is case-by-case and fact-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will investigate each complaint under §92.210 on a case-by-case basis, reviewing all applicable evidence to determine whether the covered entity identified the tool and took reasonable mitigation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will employ complaint investigations and compliance reviews (including proactive reviews based on potential complaints) to determine compliance. Investigations will examine identification, mitigation, and the specific facts surrounding alleged discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of incentives or pressure on clinicians to follow algorithmic recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will take into account whether covered entities have set up incentives that pressure health care professionals to follow recommendations of clinical algorithms even if they conflict with professional clinical judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such incentive structures are present, OCR will consider them on a case-by-case basis in determining whether a covered entity violated §92.210; this factor may affect the reasonableness of a covered entity’s mitigation and oversight practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR provision of technical assistance and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR seeks to provide technical assistance to covered entities, particularly physician practices, to help integrate clinical algorithms and algorithm improvements into clinical workflows while minimizing administrative burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR commits to partnering with covered entities to eliminate discrimination and provide clarifying guidance and technical assistance as appropriate; such assistance is meant to support compliance but is not a regulatory safe harbor unless specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed applicability / compliance timeframe for §§92.210(b) and (c)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR revised §92.1 to reflect a delayed applicability date requiring covered entities to comply with §§92.210(b) and (c) within 300 days following the effective date of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes covered entities may need time to identify covered tools and implement mitigation efforts. The rule provides the 300-day compliance window to aid implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in delivery of health programs and activities through telehealth
rubrics_metrics.description: §92.211: covered entities must not, in delivery of health programs and activities through telehealth services, discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR codified a standalone telehealth nondiscrimination provision to ensure health programs delivered via telehealth are provided in a nondiscriminatory manner. Telehealth-related effective communication and meaningful access requirements are covered by existing provisions (§§92.201, 92.202, 92.204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Codified definition of telehealth (includes audio-only and remote monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Telehealth defined in §92.4 as “use of electronic information and telecommunications technologies to support long-distance clinical health care, patient and professional health-related education, public health, and health administration,” including videoconferencing, the internet, store-and-forward imaging, streaming media, and terrestrial and wireless communications; audio-only and remote patient monitoring are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical devices, tests, and equipment used as part of telehealth services must also be accessible. OCR relied on HRSA and ONC definitions and clarified scope for regulation under §92.211.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth platforms and communications must be accessible to individuals with disabilities (unless undue burden/fundamental alteration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must ensure telehealth platforms are accessible to individuals with disabilities, unless doing so would impose undue financial and administrative burdens or result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of the health program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications before, during, and after telehealth appointments must be accessible to individuals with disabilities and individuals with limited English proficiency, consistent with section 504, title VI, and Section 1557 requirements. ICT (§92.204), effective communication (§92.202), and meaningful access (§92.201) provide baselines to tailor compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will not adopt specific accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG/Section 508) for telehealth at this time
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declined to codify WCAG 2.0 (AA), WCAG 2.1 (AA), Section 508, or related prescriptive standards for telehealth platforms in this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR cited the rapid evolution of platforms/technologies and concurrent rulemakings (by OCR and DOJ) addressing web/mobile accessibility. OCR may consider additional guidance later; covered entities must nonetheless ensure accessibility consistent with statutory obligations and may use existing standards as best practices or safe harbors if adopted in other rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio-only telehealth permitted; may require in-person alternatives as reasonable modification
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to disallow audio-only telehealth; audio-only may be essential for individuals without smartphones or reliable broadband. However, covered entities may need to offer in-person alternatives as a reasonable modification for individuals with disabilities who cannot be properly provided effective communication or for meaningful access for LEP individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will not impose a blanket requirement that in-person care be available on the same terms as telehealth, but will require reasonable modifications unless those modifications fundamentally alter the program. Complaints that require or force inappropriate telehealth delivery will be reviewed case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companions/caregivers are covered for effective communication and meaningful access
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated companions with disabilities are covered under the effective communications requirements (§92.202), and companions with LEP are covered under the meaningful access requirements (§92.201).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR determined separate telehealth language for companions was unnecessary because existing sections already cover companions; covered entities should ensure companions receive required auxiliary aids/services where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of individuals with disabilities for telehealth suitability recommended but not required
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR agrees that assessing individuals for visual, cognitive, intellectual, mobility, and functional needs would be informative and is recommended as a best practice, but declines to adopt a requirement to perform such assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities are afforded flexibility in deciding whether to assess individuals for telehealth suitability. OCR will monitor developments and may issue further guidance on assessment methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Availability requirement applies to telehealth scheduling communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic communications that inform individuals they may make telehealth appointments and that require or request a response are covered by §92.11(c)(5)(v) and thus are subject to the Notice of Availability requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities should provide Notice of Availability (as required by §92.11) when scheduling communications require a recipient response, e.g., appointment sign-ups or confirmations that solicit a reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment, reimbursement, and medical management practices must be nondiscriminatory in implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: While OCR does not set reimbursement or medical management rates, it will consider complaints that inadequate reimbursement of telehealth or disparate medical management requirements limiting access are discriminatory under Section 1557 on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practices must be implemented in a nondiscriminatory manner; OCR will evaluate whether delays or denials of telehealth access are based on prohibited grounds, including whether they constitute a discriminatory benefit design (see §92.207(b)(2)). Issues about coverage/payment generally fall outside OCR authority but will be considered when they impact access under Section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement mechanisms: applicability of referenced statutes and single administrative enforcement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §92.301 and revisions: enforcement mechanisms available under Title VI, Title IX, Section 504, and the Age Discrimination Act shall apply for purposes of Section 1557, and OCR is revising regulatory text to apply a single administrative enforcement procedure for discrimination complaints filed under Section 1557 regardless of the alleged basis of discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This unified administrative procedure is intended to simplify the complaint process for complainants and covered entities, including complaints involving multiple bases of discrimination. OCR will continue to provide resources and guidance on complaint processes and how covered entities should respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private right of action and judicial standards are matters for courts, not OCR rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have long recognized that Section 1557 authorizes a private right of action; OCR declines to revise regulatory text to adopt a stance on standards that apply to private litigants (e.g., disparate-impact standards) as that is for the Federal judiciary to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will not use rulemaking to define standards for private litigation; commenters seeking explicit rule text regarding private remedies or exhaustion requirements (e.g., Age Act administrative exhaustion) were not adopted by OCR in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will not postpone enforcement past the effective date (60 days); enforcement discretion limited
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines requests to postpone enforcement past the effective date of 60 days after publication of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1557 has been in effect since 2010; OCR expects compliance and will not delay enforcement. OCR may exercise enforcement discretion in specific cases but will not adopt a blanket postponement; covered entities should be prepared to comply beginning at the rule's effective date.
